He moved to the United States at the age of 17 to attend [[Montverde Academy]]. Alabi played [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State Seminoles]] where he was a two-time [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) All-Defensive team selection in both his freshman and sophomore years. He was selected by the [[Dallas Mavericks]] as the 50th overall pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]] and played two seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[Toronto Raptors]]. Alabi played one season in the [[NBA Development League]] and finished his career overseas with stints in Greece, Taiwan, the Philippines and Japan. ==Early life== Alabi was raised in a village near the town of [[Zaria]] in [[Kaduna State]].{{cite web |title=Alabi loving college life |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2009/11/26/alabi-loving-college-life/ |website=Orlando Sentinel |access-date=December 7, 2023 |date=August 6, 2021}} His father is a retired police officer and he has five siblings. Alabi grew up playing soccer, tennis, ping-pong, volleyball, handball and field hockey.{{cite web |last=Landman |first=Brian |title=WORKING TO MAKE HIS SHOTS COUNT |url=https://www.tampabay.com/archive/2008/12/07/working-to-make-his-shots-count/ |website=Tampa Bay Times |access-date=December 7, 2023 |date=December 9, 2008}} The only basketball court near his home was on sand and used for playing soccer.{{cite web |last1=Newberry |first1=Paul |title=Coming to America: Africans playing hoops in US |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sdut-bko-out-africa-abridged-062209-2009jun22-story.html |website=The San Diego Union Tribune |access-date=December 7, 2023 |date=June 22, 2009}} He started playing basketball during his adolescence and began to pursue it seriously once he learned that he could achieve a college scholarship by playing. Alabi attended a camp run by [[Masai Ujiri]] and earned a scholarship to attend [[Montverde Academy]]. Alabi moved to the United States in June 2005. He was coached at Montverde Academy by Kevin Sutton.{{Cite web|url=https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/who-is-solomon-alabi|title=Who Is Solomon Alabi|last=Young|first=Justin|date=2005-08-25|website=Rivals|access-date=2017-07-02}} Alabi was an all-state performer and helped lead Montverde Academy to a perfect 30–0 record as a senior.{{cite web |url=http://www.seminoles.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/alabi_solomon00.html |title=Player Bio: Solomon Alabi |publisher=Seminoles.com |access-date=2010-06-11 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111007082420/http://www.seminoles.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/alabi_solomon00.html |archive-date=2011-10-07 }} He averaged 17.5 points, 11.4 rebounds and 6 blocks per game during his senior season. ==College career== After breaking his leg 10 games into his [[freshman]] year, Alabi had to take a [[medical redshirt]]. As a redshirt freshman, he earned All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] Freshman Team honors by averaging 8.4 points per game and leading the ACC in blocks with 2.1 per game. For his great shot-blocking ability, he was named to the ACC All-Defensive team in 2008–2009. As a redshirt [[Sophomore year|sophomore]], Alabi ranked 26th in the nation in blocked shots with an average of 2.39 while increasing his scoring average to 11.7 points per game.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4268/solomon-alabi |title=Solomon Alabi Stats, News, Photos – Florida State Seminoles – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |access-date=2010-06-11}} On April 23, 2010, he declared himself eligible for the [[2010 NBA draft]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.palmbeachpost.com/sports/seminoles/fsu-sophomore-center-solomon-alabi-declares-for-nba-609550.html|archive-date=April 28, for NBA Draft}} ==Professional career== On June 24, 2010, Alabi was drafted by the [[Dallas Mavericks]] with the 50th pick, and traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] for cash considerations.{{Cite 2011.{{Cite web|url=http://www.goerie.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=2011304049920|title=Raptors recall BayHawks center Alabi}} On January 4, 2012, Alabi was assigned to the [[Bakersfield Jam]] of the D-League.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/20120104/23689/alabi-assigned-bakersfield-jam-nba-d-league|title=Alabi Assigned To Bakersfield Jam Of The NBA D-League|website=www.nba.com}} He was recalled on January 22, 2012.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/20120122/24863/alabi-recalled-bakersfield-jam|title=Alabi Recalled From Bakersfield Jam|website=www.nba.com}} Alabi's final NBA game was played on April 26, 2012, against the [[New Jersey Nets]], the final game of the regular season. In that game, Alabi recorded career highs of 11 points, 19 rebounds and 3 blocks in 40 minutes.[http://www.nba.com/games/20120426/NJNTOR/gameinfo.html Uzoh has triple-double as Raptors rout Nets] On October 1, 2012, Solomon signed with the [[New Orleans Hornets]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-add-three-players|title=HORNETS ADD THREE PLAYERS|website=[[NBA.com]] }} However, he was released on October 27, four days before the Hornets' season opener.{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-waive-alabi-wright|title=HORNETS WAIVE ALABI, WRIGHT|website=[[NBA.com]] }} On December 28, 2012, Alabi joined the [[Idaho Stampede]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/idaho/solomon_alabi_acquired_201213_2012_12_28.html|title=STAMPEDE ACQUIRE ALABI|website=[[NBA.com]] }} He was released on March 1, 2013. On March 21, 2013, he signed with the Greek first division basketball club [[Ikaros Kallitheas B.C.]] On September 28, 2013, Alabi signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/2013/09/sixers-add-solomon-alabi-and-nayal-koshwal-to-training-camp-roster/|title=Sixers add Solomon Alabi and Nayal Koshwal to training camp roster – NBA Blog – NBA Basketball Blog|date=September 28, 2013}} However, he was waived on October 5.{{Cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/2013/10/sixers-sign-gani-lawal-waive-solomon-alabi/|title=Sixers sign Gani Lawal, waive Solomon Alabi – NBA Blog – NBA Basketball Blog|date=October 5, 2013}} He later signed with the [[Yulon Dinos]] of Taiwan for the 2013–14 season. In January 2015, Alabi signed with the [[Barako Bull Energy]] for the [[2015 PBA Commissioner's Cup]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.philstar.com/sports/2015/01/04/1409285/another-7-footer-invade-pba|title=Another 7-footer to invade PBA|first=Joaquin M.|last=Henson|website=Philstar.com}} Alabai retired from his basketball career in 2018 to spend more time with his family.{{cite web |last1=Cassidy |first1=Benjamin |title=Meet the Former NBA Player Turned Seattle Real Estate Agent |url=https://www.seattlemet.com/home-and-real-estate/2021/08/former-toronto-raptors-nba-player-turned-seattle-real-estate-agent |website=Seattle Met |access-date=December 7, 2023 |date=August 16, 2021}} == National team career == Alabi started for the Nigerian Junior National Team at the 2007 Nike All-American camp. He also helped Nigeria qualify for the [[2007 FIBA Under-19 World Championship]]. He was selected for the 2007 [[Nike Hoop Summit]], representing the World Select Team, where he led all players in blocked shots.{{Cite news|url=http://archive.usab.com/mens/hoopsummit/hsum_2007.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150115224722/http://archive.usab.com/mens/hoopsummit/hsum_2007.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=January They have lived in [[Seattle, Washington]], since 2015. Alabi returned to [[Florida State University]] and graduated in 2020 with a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in interdisciplinary social science.{{cite web |title=Basketball's Alabi Earns Degree At Florida State Commencement |url=https://seminoles.com/news/2020/12/11/basketballs-alabi-earns-degree-at-florida-state-commencement |website=Florida State University |access-date=December 7, 2023 |date=December 11, 2020}} Alabi has worked as a real estate agent in Seattle since 2020. ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== *{{Basketballstats |nba= 202374 |bbr= a/alabiso01 }} *[https://web.archive.org/web/20141024065456/http://stats.nbadleague.com/playerProfile.html?PlayerID=202374 NBA D-League Profile] {{2010 NBA draft}} {{B2 League rebounding leaders}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Alabi, Solomon}} [[Category:1988 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Barako Bull Energy players]] [[Category:Bakersfield Jam players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Orlando, Florida]] [[Category:Centers (basketball)]] [[Category:Dallas Mavericks draft picks]] [[Category:Erie BayHawks (2008–2017) players]] [[Category:Florida State Seminoles men's basketball players]] [[Category:Fukushima Firebonds players]] [[Category:Idaho Stampede players]] [[Category:Ikaros B.C. players]] [[Category:Montverde Academy alumni]] [[Category:NBA players from Nigeria]] [[Category:Nigerian expatriate basketball people in Japan]] [[Category:Nigerian expatriate basketball people in the Philippines]] [[Category:Nigerian expatriate basketball people in the United States]] [[Category:Nigerian men's basketball players]] [[Category:People from Zaria]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Kaduna State]] [[Category:Philippine Basketball Association imports]] [[Category:Super Basketball League imports]] [[Category:Toronto Raptors players]] [[Category:Fighting Eagles Nagoya players]] [[Category:Yulon (basketball) players]] [[Category:21st-century Nigerian sportsmen]]
